_transcription: ENGLISH PAGES = the EVEN 0-based indices 2, 4 and 6 — only three of them, because this is the 40-mark Term-2 paper. ALL EIGHT rendered indices were opened and accounted for, not just the even ones: idx 0 cover (Series ABCD5/5, SET No. 1, Q.P. Code 65/5/1, 'contains 7 printed pages', 'contains 14 questions', 2 hours / 40 marks); idx 1 HINDI General Instructions + Hindi Q1-Q5; idx 2 ENGLISH General Instructions + SECTION A Q1-Q5; idx 3 HINDI Q6-Q10; idx 4 ENGLISH Q6 (a)/(b) + SECTION B Q7-Q10; idx 5 HINDI Q11-Q14; idx 6 ENGLISH SECTION C Q11-Q14; idx 7 BLANK apart from the QR code and the '65/5/1 8' footer. That map is confirmed a second, independent way by out/2022-65-5-1/contact.png, the pipeline's own contact sheet — an idx-labelled thumbnail grid of all eight pages, which shows the language of every page at a glance and agrees with the page-by-page read exactly. It is worth opening FIRST on any paper in this pipeline: it settles the language/parity question in one look before a single full page is read. The alternation is per CHUNK, not per question: each language block runs a whole page and the two languages happen to need exactly one page each per chunk, so 'even indices are English' holds — but it was checked page by page rather than assumed. NO English overflow onto any odd page and no parity inversion: idx 3 opens directly on Hindi '6. (क)' and idx 4 opens directly on English '6. (a)', so the English Q5->Q6 hand-off jumps the Hindi page cleanly, and idx 5 opens on the Hindi 'खण्ड ग' heading. Question numbers run 1-14 unbroken with every sub-part present. FOLIO/COVER MISMATCH, same class as the 2026 65/3/1 note in the brief: the cover says 7 printed pages and the last folio reads 8 (idx 7 is a blank eighth page). INTERNAL CHOICE = FOUR (Q6, Q8, Q10, Q13). Instruction (vi) prints NO count ('There is an internal choice in some questions.'), so this was established by walking the OFFICIAL MARKING SCHEME question by question — it reprints each question block and then both branches under 'Or': Q6 has A6(a)/A6(b) [ms idx 4], Q8 has A8.(a)/A8.(b) [ms idx 5], Q10 has A10.(a)/A10.(b) [ms idx 6-7], Q13 has A13.(a)/A13.(b) [ms idx 8-9]. Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q7, Q9, Q11, Q12 and Q14 each have a single answer block with no 'Or' — a checked absence, not an assumed one. Q14 is NOT an internal choice: its (a) and (b) are genuine SUB-PARTS of 2 marks each and the scheme marks BOTH (A14.(a) and A14.(b), no 'Or' between them). Cross-check on marks: primary branches 5x2 + 2 (Q6) = 12 in A, 4x3 = 12 in B, 3x4 + 4 (Q14) = 16 in C, total 40, matching the cover — but per the brief that sum is structurally blind to a MISSED alternative, which is why the scheme walk is what the count rests on. NO MCQs ANYWHERE, confirmed: all 14 questions are free-response, so every row is 'subjective', no row carries options or an 'answer', and the blind MCQ key re-derivation that anchors 2023-2026 cannot run on this paper at all. Decimal points are BASELINE full stops in this question paper — verified on a 3x crop of idx 6: Q11 prints '0.8, 0.5 and 0.3' with ordinary periods, so they are transcribed '0.8' and NOT '0{\cdot}8'. The MARKING SCHEME disagrees with its own paper and prints them RAISED in A11 ('0·2, 0·5, 0·7'); the paper wins, the same QP-vs-MS split recorded for 2023 65/5/1. plan.txt says 'No reference papers given - transcribe every question', so all 19 rows were transcribed from scratch and nothing was skipped. NO solutions written for any row, per the brief. TWO ITEMS FOR THE NEXT AGENT. (1) Q6(a) is a genuine CBSE defect — its three given probabilities are mutually inconsistent and the official scheme does not notice; see the _flag on Q6a, and expect the same block in sibling 65/5 sets. (2) Q9 asks for the equation of a PLANE — the NCERT rationalisation gap config.ts warns about for exactly this pre-rationalisation paper. It was first filed on the closest available subtopic with a _flag, and has since been MOVED to the new 'The Plane' subtopic (Three Dimensional Geometry, order_index 5) added to the live axis on 2026-08-19 after several 2022 agents hit the same gap; the flag is dropped, since the mismatch it named is resolved. Q9 is the ONLY plane question on this paper — Q5 is direction cosines and Q14 (a)/(b) are both about the two given LINES (shortest distance, then their point of intersection), so neither belongs on 'The Plane'. ALSO NOTED, affecting no row: the marking scheme's A12 working prints an incoherent penultimate line, '= 1/2 + [4 - 4/2 - 2 + 1/2]' followed by '= -1 + 2 = 1'; the bracket evaluates to 1/2 and the stated final area 1 is correct, so this is a typesetting slip inside CBSE's own solution, not a question defect.

questions.stem:
Find the general solution of the following differential equation :

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{x-y} + x^2 e^{-y}\)

Let X be a random variable which assumes values \(x_1\), \(x_2\), \(x_3\), \(x_4\) such that \(2P(X = x_1) = 3P(X = x_2) = P(X = x_3) = 5P(X = x_4)\).

Find the probability distribution of X.
If a line makes an angle \(\alpha\), \(\beta\), \(\gamma\) with the coordinate axes, then find the value of \(\cos 2\alpha + \cos 2\beta + \cos 2\gamma\).

Events A and B are such that

\(P(A) = \dfrac{1}{2}\), \(P(B) = \dfrac{7}{12}\) and \(P\left(\overline{A} \cup \overline{B}\right) = \dfrac{1}{4}\)

Find whether the events A and B are independent or not.
questions._flag: CBSE DEFECT — the three given probabilities are MUTUALLY INCONSISTENT. Verified on a 2.6x crop of page idx 4: the bars are printed over A and over B SEPARATELY (two bars with a clear gap at the union sign), so the given quantity is \(P(\overline{A} \cup \overline{B})\) and De Morgan gives \(P(A \cap B) = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4\) — which exceeds \(P(A) = 1/2\) and is therefore impossible for any pair of events. The official marking scheme performs exactly that step (A6(a) writes \(P(\overline{A} \cup \overline{B}) = P(\overline{A \cap B}) = 1 - P(A \cap B)\), then \(P(A \cap B) = 3/4\)) and does NOT notice the contradiction; it concludes 'not independent' by comparing 3/4 against \(P(A)P(B) = 7/24\). Transcribed exactly as printed. Note the reading \(P(\overline{A \cup B}) = 1/4\) — a single bar spanning the union — would be consistent (it gives \(P(A \cap B) = 1/3 \ne 7/24\), same verdict), but that is NOT what either document prints and it is not adopted here.

questions.stem: A box \(B_1\) contains 1 white ball and 3 red balls. Another box \(B_2\) contains 2 white balls and 3 red balls. If one ball is drawn at random from each of the boxes \(B_1\) and \(B_2\), then find the probability that the two balls drawn are of the same colour.

If \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) are two vectors such that \(\left|\vec{a} + \vec{b}\right| = \left|\vec{b}\right|\), then prove that \(\left(\vec{a} + 2\vec{b}\right)\) is perpendicular to \(\vec{a}\).

If \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) are unit vectors and \(\theta\) is the angle between them, then prove that

\(\sin \dfrac{\theta}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left|\vec{a} - \vec{b}\right|\).

Find the equation of the plane passing through the line of intersection of the planes \(\vec{r} \cdot \left(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}\right) = 10\) and \(\vec{r} \cdot \left(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - \hat{k}\right) + 4 = 0\) and passing through the point \((-2, 3, 1)\).

Three persons A, B and C apply for a job of manager in a private company. Chances of their selection are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 4. The probability that A, B and C can introduce changes to increase the profits of a company are 0.8, 0.5 and 0.3 respectively. If increase in the profit does not take place, find the probability that it is due to the appointment of A.

questions.stem: Find the area bounded by the curves \(y = |x - 1|\) and \(y = 1\), using integration.

Solve the following differential equation :

\(\left(y - \sin^2 x\right) dx + \tan x\, dy = 0\)

Find the general solution of the differential equation :

\(\left(x^3 + y^3\right) dy = x^2 y\, dx\)
